analysis.title: How the Blue Wave Bull could rewrite the current correlation playbook
key_insights: Average 20-day realized cross-asset correlation has collapsed toward zero heading into the midterm results, its lowest level in years (UBS). Established hedges may behave differently as a new political regime is priced in.
The SPX/rates correlation has reversed sharply back toward the classic risk-off configuration, so stocks and yields can fall together again (UBS).

Brent and the ratio of crossover to investment-grade European credit spreads have moved closely together throughout 2026, and both rebounded sharply from summer lows (Goldman). The report flags this as a relationship to watch for a break.
The S&P 500 Low Volatility Index has its most negative correlation with the Nasdaq for this time of year in more than three decades (Peter Callahan).

Semiconductor exposure in the S&P 500 has fallen from almost 20% to around 16%, still historically elevated. Concentration is starting to ease and a change in leadership could change the index's correlation profile (Strategas, Todd Sohn).
Ex-AI equities show about 10% correlation with the S&P 500. The AI/ex-AI basket has about 60% correlation with the index and negative 30% correlation with long Treasuries (Fidelity, Jurrien Timmer).

The rolling one-month correlation between AI-related equities and 10-year Treasury yields is climbing back toward +0.6, while the correlation with Brent has turned negative (Goldman). Rates now matter more to AI equities than oil does.
The report cautions that it may be a bad time to assume pre-election correlations will hold after the midterms.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Lowest in years. Diversification and hedge relationships are less reliable going into the post-election regime.

macro_indicators.interpretation: AI equities are trading as a rates-sensitive group, more so than as an oil-sensitive one.

The Brent vs crossover/IG credit spread ratio relationship could break as the political and macro backdrop shifts.
Semiconductor concentration is easing, which could change the index's correlation profile.
